articles.title: Gerwyn Price wins last-leg thriller against Niko Springer at Grand Slam of Darts to set up semi-final against Kevin Doets
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price survived match darts from Niko Springer to make it through to the semi-finals; he will take on Kevin Doets, who defeated Jermaine Wattimena; watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
It was a staggering encounter in which Springer would just not go away. That paid dividends when, for the first time in 29 legs, Springer took the lead at 15-14.

Price took out a clutch 143 finish to send the match all the way and in the final leg, Springer went low on D4 for 73 in a missed match dart.

That gave Price his chance at 78 and with T18 followed by D12, he was through to another major semi-final.

The Welshman is aiming for his fourth Grand Slam of Darts title, adding to his 2018, 2019 and 2021 victories.

He takes on Kevin Doets after an inspired display from the Dutchman which saw him hit two Big Fish and reel off 10 legs in a row in a 16-7 routing of Jermaine Wattimena.

"I'm probably quite lucky to come through that game. I missed so many chances. I should have punished him and being so far in front, but I kept him in the game," Price told Sky Sports .

"I kept missing doubles after doubles, even though he was scoring as well as I was.

"I was missing opportunities after opportunities. But I've got to add another one at the end.

"I'm pleased now but if I lost that game, you know what it's like.

"It's a game that you shouldn't lose and I felt like it's a game I shouldn't have lost anyway. I missed so many opportunities."

Early on it looked like three-time Grand Slam champion Price was playing in a way that his opponent would potentially not be able to keep up with as he broke the German in the first leg and then broke twice more and took four legs in a row for a 7-3 lead.

Springer was averaging over 104 but he still could not get within touching distance.

Despite Price's levels, Springer would not give up and in the third session he started to make big inroads. By taking out three of the five legs available, he drew the match closer to 11-9.

It looked like Price was going to run away again as he took a four-leg lead at 13-9 up but as was the story of the tale, back came Springer once again with the match turning edgy and doubling becoming troublesome.

A run of three legs on the spin brought Springer within one leg of Price and then a burst of two more finally saw him level at 14-14.

It was then in the 29th leg that Springer took the lead for the first time in the contest but in classic 'Iceman' style, he pinned a sensational 143 finish to take the quarter-final all the way.

Even in that deciding leg, Springer had a chance to take the match but a low dart on D4 allowed Price to check out 78.

Kevin Doets put in a stunning performance and stormed into his first TV semi-final with a 16-7 victory over his friend Jermaine Wattimena, taking out 10 legs in a row and reeling in two 'Big Fish' finishes on the way.

Doets averaged 102.63, had 46 per cent on the doubles, eight 180s and 15 140s in a complete performance.

Wattimena had the early advantage thanks to some incredible doubling and a break of throw that had him 3-2 up after the early exchanges.

But after a second blistering mini session, in which Doets averaged over 114, he had levelled the game at 5-5.

It was from that stunning standard that Doets made his move. Rattling off six legs in a row, Doets punished a bust score from Wattimena for a break of throw and then reeled in the Big Fish for another.

In the blink of an eye, he was 10-5 up and Wattimena was floundering.

Doets was on a magnificent roll and made it all the way to 14-5 ahead and 10 legs in a row before Wattimena finally stopped the rot, a second sensational 170 finish showing the ridiculous levels that Doets was reaching.

While Wattimena got a consolatory two legs back, Doets came back, broke the throw, and then finished on D18 to make it to the final four on his Grand Slam debut.

"I feel right now like an elite player, but you're not part of the elite if you haven't won anything," Doets told Sky Sports .

"I have won a floor tournament but it's not the elite yet.

"I'm working towards it. I'm touching them. I'm very close but not yet."

articles.title: WWE SmackDown Live Updates, Results and Highlights From November 20
articles.summary: Welcome to B/R's coverage of the November 20 episode of WWE SmackDown.
articles.body:
Say what you will of the build to Survivor Series and the Team USA vs. Team Mexico elimination tag team match, but the chemistry that Punk and Rhodes have flashed, and their comedic timing, has been one of the bright spots of WWE TV in recent weeks.

The "aside" that they held in the ring, while talking about Hacksaw Duggan's ability to wrestle at Survivor Series, was one of the funniest things seen on Raw, SmackDown, or any other WWE programming all year.

That they can switch it off and get serious when the time calls for it, such as the end-of-show tease for Monday's broadcast, only makes it that much better.

Also, given Punk's reaction, it feels like a certain Visionary may be on his way back.

With Survivor Series just eight days away, hyping the card and its matches was a necessity, and WWE did that near-perfectly here. The Women's War Games match got its time and the Team USA vs. Team Mexico match dominated the airwaves as it was featured prominently across several segments.

At this time last year, despite questionable losses, Gunther still had the air of a killer. He was a dangerous force between the ropes, with the ability to beat and retire anyone at any time, including John Cena.

Fast forward 11 months, and The Ring General feels like an also-ran, a guy whose prominence on the show has been minimized and whose invincibility all but erased.

He has earned better than that, as have all of the Superstars sacrificed to help him build that aura.

articles.title: Gukesh-Sindarov clash puts India-Uzbek chess rivalry in focus
articles.summary: PUNE: The World Championship match that starts on Tuesday in Geneva, Switzerland, is not just about reigning champion D Gukesh and challenger Javokhir
articles.body: PUNE: The World Championship match that starts on Tuesday in Geneva, Switzerland, is not just about reigning champion D Gukesh and challenger Javokhir Sindarov. It's also about India and Uzbekistan.Uzbekistan, a part of the former Soviet bloc, has a strong Russian influence. The players speak Russian and, although belonging to a new nation, started to make their mark around the same time as V Anand in the late 1980s.More importantly, Uzbeks work as a team. How else could one explain having only 21 GMs and only 10 active GMs above Elo 2500 and still winning an Olympiad gold twice in the last three editions?Their second-best player Nodirbek Abdusattorov is openly helping Sindarov, with coach IM Roman Vidonyak and second GM Mukhiddin Madaminov forming a core group. They are also confident that Abdusattorov’s recent camp with Magnus Carlsen will help them further.Gukesh has got none other than V Anand’s mentorship and the five-time world champion’s former second Grzegorz Gajewski. Anand’s former second Rustam Kasimdzhanov, whom the Indian legend had defeated in the 2002 World Cup final in Hyderabad, is Uzbekistan’s current national coach.Gukesh tried to add to this intrigue by going with Norway Chess champion R Praggnanandhaa and his women’s world championship challenger sister R Vaishali to a movie. His full team will be known only later on.Though Ding Liren was not in top-form against Gukesh in their world title match two years ago, he probably showed better fighting spirit and ability to convert than the Indian in their match in Singapore a couple of years ago. However, the last-game blunder proved to be the Chinese’s undoing. Gukesh is unlikely to get such a gift from Sindarov unless the fellow 20-year-old is forced into severe time trouble.At the Olympiad, the Uzbeks had held the Indians twice — in 2022 when Gukesh lost to Abdusattorov and 2024 — and beat them once, in Samarkand this year.Clearly, the Indians have found the Uzbeks to be a tough nut to crack.The tiny nation with a population of about four crore boasts of 21 Grandmasters. In comparison, Gukesh’s home state of Tamil Nadu alone has 38 GMs among a population of 8 crore.But one gets an impression that Uzbeks are products of the system and work together better.On the other hand, Gukesh belongs to the school of individual brilliance boosted by private initiatives.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I  don't want to play': Magnus Carlsen says his entry at Total Chess Pilot was 'unfortunate'
articles.summary: Magnus Carlsen has admitted that he was not in the right frame of mind to compete at the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest, saying his
articles.body: Magnus Carlsen has admitted that he was not in the right frame of mind to compete at the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest, saying his participation in the tournament had been "unfortunate". The five-time world champion also said he was frustrated with the way people in the chess world questioned his statements.Carlsen made the comments in an interview with TV2 Norge after winning the second blitz game against Vladislav Artemiev on Thursday. Asked about the controversy surrounding him at the tournament, the Norwegian said, "It annoys me a little, everything that's happening. I can say more generally, what annoys me the absolute most in the chess world is that people do not believe me on what I say. I always speak exactly what I think and exactly how I intend it."Explaining his concerns about taking part in the event, Carlsen said he had been away from his family for a long time and was not keen to play tournaments unless there was a significant sporting or financial incentive."When it's about this tournament I'll say that my entry was unfortunate," he said, as quoted by ChessBase."I was not in the state of playing chess right now, because it's a long time to be away from my family right now. And it's a point in my career where I necessarily don't want to play tournaments where there's not a lot of stakes, where it's either very important or very lucrative. And here this was more stressful than fun. And of course that's a bad entry to have to a tournament, and then everything gets very amplified when I was not very motivated to begin with," Carlsen said.Magnus Carlsen's high-stakes gamble pays offCarlsen took an unusual route to protecting his place at the top of world chess, forfeiting two games against Vladislav Artemiev before producing a must-win performance in the Fast Classic to secure his first victory in the format at the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest on Thursday.The five-time world champion, competing for 17th place, turned a 3-9 deficit into an 11-9 victory, winning the Fast Classic game to complete an extraordinary comeback. The result also lifted his live rating to 2804, keeping him above the coveted 2,800 Elo mark and retaining his world No. 1 status.After skipping his Fast Classic games against Bibisara Assaubayeva for two consecutive days, Carlsen chose to sit out of the rapid section this time against Vladislav Artemiev.Carlsen had won three of the four blitz games, but forfeited both rapid games, leaving him needing the eight-point Fast Classic win to take the day.With the win, Carlsen's live rating also improved to 2804.Carlsen's rating and ranking were genuinely under threat. A draw against Artemiev in the Fast Classic would have taken his rating down to 2799, marking the first time in 17 years that he would have fallen below 2,800. A defeat, coupled with a win for Fabiano Caruana, would also have opened the door for the American to become world No. 1.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: India’s campaign at the Hong Kong Open Super 500 gathered momentum on Friday.
articles.body: India’s campaign at the Hong Kong Open Super 500 gathered momentum on Friday. The men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty and in-form Lakshya Sen stormed into the semifinals with impressive victories. But Rakshitha Ramraj’s dream run ended in the women’s singles quarterfinals. articles.title: LSU women's basketball star MiLaysia Fulwiley faces only misdemeanor charges after arrest
articles.summary: LSU's MiLaysia Fulwiley faces only misdemeanor fleeing and resisting charges after her arrest, with felony counts dropped and a diversion program planned.
articles.body: LSU women’s basketball player MiLaysia Fulwiley will face misdemeanor traffic citations stemming from a recent traffic incident. The felony charges included in her initial booking will now be pursued as misdemeanor counts, the East Baton Rouge District Attorney's Office confirmed Friday. Authorities allege Fulwiley attempted to evade officers during a traffic stop. District Attorney Hillar Moore said fleeing and resisting an officer would be weighed as misdemeanors. Fulwiley will also be referred to a diversion program to resolve the charges. The initial charges listed at the time of Fulwiley’s booking included aggravated battery and assault, based on allegations that she drove her vehicle into an officer’s vehicle. Fulwiley has denied the police's account. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE State police captain Russell Graham said Friday that his agency reviewed evidence with Moore and agreed with his decision. "After a thorough review with all involved parties, the charges were amended based on the circumstances and evidence presented," State Police said in a written statement provided by Graham. Fulwiley has not appeared in a game for LSU since her arrest. It remains unclear whether she will return to the team. ALABAMA DISMISSES DEFENSIVE BACK DRE KIRKPATRICK JR FROM TEAM AFTER BEING ARRESTED FOR SECOND TIME Fulwiley apologized to police and her teammates. "Saturday night ended in a situation that never should have happened," she said in a statement released by LSU. "I owe an apology to the officers involved and everyone who calls themselves a Tiger. I also want to apologize to my family and all those who love and support me." The traffic stop happened near Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge as the a football game between LSU and Texas was ending. "Rules and laws apply to everyone, including the instructions of officers working a game night in Baton Rouge," Fulwiley said. "I respect the job those officers do, and I’ll let the legal process run its course. My focus is doing what this program asks of me and earning back the trust of the people who count on me." articles.title: Turnovers, third-down woes sink Iowa State
articles.summary: ORLANDO, Fla. — Aiden Flora broke a 62-yard touchdown sprint and recorded 171 rushing yards to climb into fifth place for the most single-season rushing yard...
articles.body:
ORLANDO, Fla. — Aiden Flora broke a 62-yard touchdown sprint and recorded 171 rushing yards to climb into fifth place for the most single-season rushing yards in Iowa State history, but uncharacteristic fumbles and execution struggles doomed the Cyclones in a 48-17 loss to UCF on Friday night.

Flora set the pace early for Iowa State after UCF won the coin toss and deferred to the second half. The Cyclones opened the game on offense with a 12-play drive, taking a 3-0 lead when Kyle Konrardy booted a 27-yard field goal at the 8:31 mark of the first quarter. Flora touched the football on nine of those 12 plays during a series extended by facemask and pass interference penalties against the Knights.

UCF tied the score 3-3 at 3:28 in the opening quarter on Will Stone's 24-yard field goal. The Knights' drive featured two pass completions of 15-plus yards and five rushes of four-plus yards, though Tyren Hornes dropped a potential touchdown pass in the end zone before UCF settled for three points. Penalties for an ineligible receiver downfield on Braden Smith and holding on Maasai King stalled Iowa State's second possession. DuPont executed a 41-yard punt to set UCF up at its own 40-yard line, and the Knights gained 29 yards in three plays to close the first quarter at the Cyclones' 26-yard line.

UCF pulled ahead 10-3 at 13:09 of the second quarter when Alonza Barnett III connected with Josh Derry on a 21-yard touchdown pass near the "S" in the Knights' end zone logo to finish a seven-play, 60-yard drive in 2:44. Iowa State looked poised to counter, but Flora fumbled after gaining 13 yards on a catch, giving UCF possession at its own 25-yard line. Iowa Western transfer Blake Hawkins sacked Barnett on the final play of the second quarter, but UCF held a 24-10 advantage at halftime.

Derry extended UCF's lead to 31-10 at 11:11 in the third quarter by snaring his third touchdown reception of the night. Iowa State responded at the 9:55 mark when Flora broke free for a 62-yard touchdown run, pulling the Cyclones within 31-17 following Konrardy's extra point.

The Cyclones defense gave Iowa State a window of opportunity by forcing UCF's first punt of the evening and later holding when Stone missed a 29-yard field goal—his second miss of the night—giving Iowa State the ball at its own 11-yard line with 2:10 left in the third quarter. However, Iowa State suffered another lost fumble. Entering the contest, Iowa State had lost just three fumbles all season, ranking second in the Big 12 and 16th nationally.

UCF converted the turnover into a 2-yard touchdown run by Duane Thomas Jr. at 14:25 of the fourth quarter to push the lead to 38-17. Iowa State struggled on conversion downs, finishing 1-for-10 on third down and 0-for-2 on fourth down.

Statistically, Iowa State accumulated 298 net total yards (189 rushing, 109 passing) across 57 plays, averaging 5.2 yards per play with 15 total first downs (nine rushing, three passing, three penalty). UCF recorded 460 net total yards (205 rushing, 255 passing) across 69 plays, averaging 6.7 yards per play with 23 first downs.

Stone added a 38-yard field goal for UCF at 9:27, and the Knights sealed the victory at 6:35 of the fourth quarter when center Jacob Maiava caught a 5-yard touchdown pass.

Iowa State takes on Kansas State on Nov. 28 at 1 p.m.

articles.title: No. 1 Michigan hockey brawls, beats rival Michigan State
articles.summary: As the Wolverines pulled away late, the two schools showed there's no love lost between the two.
articles.body:
ANN ARBOR -- With 13 minutes left in the third period Friday at Yost Arena, the primary beatdown had already been delivered. Now it was time to get extracurricular.

With the No. 1 Michigan hockey team leading 5-1 in the third period, senior forward Nick Moldenhauer was blindsided by a hit off the puck from No. 9 Michigan State sophomore defenseman Sean Barnhill. What ensued was an all-out brawl, starting near the boards where the initial incident occurred and spilling over towards the Wolverines bench, where anyone who wasn't yet involved was given a prime opportunity.

Referees spent multiple minutes attempting to pull the embittered rivals apart as haymakers flew, wrestling matches commenced and jerseys ripped. Multiple fights were quelled momentarily by a not-so-brotherly hug, only to resume at the slightest flinch. When green and maize was finally pulled apart, the result was mass ejections of key contributors to both squads, but it really only hurt the squad that started it.

As Wolverines forward Nic Sima exited the ice for the night, disqualified by the brawl, he threw his arms in the air to pump up the crowd. By that point, it didn't matter who was on the ice, Michigan (11-1 overall, 4-1 Big Ten) had already handled the Spartans (6-4-1, 0-2-1) to take a win in the first matchup of the season, 5-1.

Before the physical onslaught Friday night, it was the pair of prodigious goaltenders that were under siege. The Wolverines' sheer quantity broke through the Spartans' defenses much more often, resulting in a clobbering no punch could make up for.

Michigan State freshman goaltender Joshua Ravensbergen was the first under siege. Michigan peppered him with an astonishing 21 shots on goal in the first period, and while he managed to get his pads out in front of the vast majority, he could only delay the inevitable result of such a high quantity for so long.

Six minutes into the contest, Ravensbergen had already made 10 saves to keep his slate clean, but none granted him refuge from the onslaught. The Wolverines were quick to catch rebounds off their own looks, and they finally took advantage when freshman center Jack Nesbitt caught the deflection from freshman Landon DuPont's strike, slotting the first goal of the contest over Ravensberger's shoulder.

Now that their barrage was yielding results, the Wolverines kept their foot on the gas, and six minutes later, fellow freshman J.P Hurlbert doubled Michigan's early lead. The freshmen didn't seem to have too much trouble adapting to their first edition of the in-state rivalry.

Michigan State was severely outshot in the first 20 minutes, putting only nine shots of its own on goal, but found luck off a last-minute faceoff in Michigan territory. Junior forward Cullen Potter caught Jack Hextall's pass from behind the net to punch in a Spartan goal with just 21 seconds left in the period.

The late Michigan State attack was a sign of things to come for Jack Ivankovic, who soon undertook his own bombardment following the intermission. The Spartans flipped the offensive script on its head, turning a 21-9 shot deficit into 27-25 by the second horn. Ivankovic was pressured as hard in the second as Ravensbergen was in the first, except for one difference: he held the line.

Eleven minutes into the second period, Ravensbergen made an expert stop on a one-on-one opportunity from sophomore forward Aidan Park, and the Spartans' offense did its best to pay him back. They skated right down into Michigan territory, firing five shots off in the span of 13 seconds trying to penetrate Ivankovic's defense. He stopped them all. A similar barrage came with just about two minutes left in the period as Michigan State fired another round of consecutive shots to no avail.

WIth full confidence in their last line of defense, the Wolverines top-ranked offense fully spread its wings. Michigan responded to the Spartan's only score with an additional three of its own, ballooning its lead to 5-1 just before Moldenhauer was laid out, and hockey stopped being top-of-mind for either team.

The 10 minutes of the contest flew by as the score remained still, the focus remaining on what had quickly become a precariously chippy affair. Anchored by a still-fortified Ivankovic, Michigan closed out its 5-1 win. Everyone ended up taking their lashings Friday, but it was Ivankovic's ability to sustain his own that left the Spartans blue and black.

articles.title: Mitchell scores 13 points sending Iona past UMKC 62-61
articles.summary: (AP) — Keyshawn Mitchell scored 13 points as Iona beat UMKC 62-61 on Friday.Aiden Disu made 1 of 2 foul shots with two seconds left.
articles.body:
NEW ROCHELLE, N.Y. (AP) — Keyshawn Mitchell scored 13 points as Iona beat UMKC 62-61 on Friday.

Aiden Disu made 1 of 2 foul shots with two seconds left. He missed the second free throw, but teammate Alliou Fall grabbed the offensive rebound to seal the win.

Mitchell also contributed eight rebounds for the Gaels (3-4). Kevon Vanderhorst scored 13 points and added five rebounds and five assists. Ore Odutayo had 12 points and went 4 of 8 from the field (2 for 4 from 3-point range).

Lincoln Goodwin led the Roos (3-4) in scoring, finishing with 19 points. Assane Diop added 15 points and 10 rebounds for UMKC. Carl Daughtery Jr. also had nine points.

articles.title: CB West tops CR South in district football semifinal
articles.summary: Central Bucks West defeats Council Rock South, earns spot in PIAA District One Class 6A football championship game.
articles.body:
DOYLESTOWN — Central Bucks West and Council Rock South had their sights set on a spot in the PIAA District One Class 6A championship game going into Friday night.

The Bucks were hoping to qualify for their second district title game since advancing to the state final in 2000, while the Golden Hawks wanted to play in their second district championship game (also 2011) since the school opened in 2002.

CB West (12-1) moved on with a 30-13 victory at War Memorial Field, earning a home date with Spring-Ford for the title Nov. 27 as the Rams won 17-14 over top seed Downingtown East in the other semifinal matchup. Senior fullback Nick Miletto scored three rushing touchdowns for the Bucks after a scoreless first quarter.

The second-seeded Bucks downed Perkiomen Valley 56-42 and intradistrict rival Central Bucks East 44-21 in the first two rounds of districts, while the No. 11 Golden Hawks topped Downingtown West 28-7 and defending district champ North Penn 20-13.

articles.title: Fans will appreciate White Sox players supporting Bulls
articles.summary: The Chicago Bulls not only welcomed the Washington Wizards on Friday night, but also the White Sox. More than a month after the White Sox were eliminated in...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls not only welcomed the Washington Wizards on Friday night, but also the White Sox. More than a month after the White Sox were eliminated in the postseason , their basketball brethren embraced them.

Two players, Mike Vasil and Chase Meidroth, took a picture with Matas Buzelis before the game. All three exchanged jerseys. Then, Vasil and Meidroth took a picture together at center court.

Vasil is a right-handed relief pitcher who finished 5-3 with a 2.50 ERA and 82 strikeouts. Meidroth is a second baseman who finished with a .276 batting average, 156 hits, 16 home runs, and 63 RBIs.

The White Sox overachieved this season. They overcame three consecutive 100+ loss seasons to reach the postseason for the first time since 2021. In the end, White Sox manager Will Venable was named AL manager of the year .

Meanwhile, the Bulls are facing the Wizards, who are 4-10. They are coming off an eight-game losing streak and are looking to string together victories, even without Caleb Wilson due to a broken hand .

The Bulls and the White Sox share a mutual history. The Reinsdorf family owns both. At the same time, they have also had periods of overlapping success.

In 1993, Michael Jordan and the Bulls won their third straight title. That same year, the White Sox made it to the ALCS, losing to the Toronto Blue Jays. As the Southsiders made their playoff run, Jordan announced his first retirement. Months later, he wore White Sox colors as he attempted a comeback in minor league baseball.

The Bulls play the Denver Nuggets at home on Sunday.

articles.title: Kansas State basketball shocked at home by Campbell
articles.summary: The goodwill Kansas State basketball built after dropping its season opener disappeared in a loss to Campbell.
articles.body:
MANHATTAN — The goodwill Kansas State built since dropping its season opener evaporated on Friday night at Bramlage Coliseum.

The Wildcats were shocked in an 80-70 loss to Campbell on Friday, Nov. 20, in Manhattan. K-State entered the game on a three-game winning streak and as a 16 1/2 point favorite to beat the Coastal Athletic Association opponent .

The loss precedes the Wildcats' most challenging slate of non-conference play when they travel to Las Vegas for the Players Era 16 tournament . They start by playing No. 19 Gonzaga on Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 11:30 p.m., before playing either No. 15 Alabama or RV Baylor on Thanksgiving.

Check out our Kansas State basketball vs Campbell photo gallery, best images

Campbell took control in the second half when it made seven consecutive shots during a 13-2 run that put the Fighting Camels up by 18 midway through the final period. The closest K-State came for the remainder of the night was within five with 53.1 seconds left after a late 10-0 run.

Lance Waddles and Rashawn Inglemon led the way for the Camels, each scoring 23 points. The Camels were 7-for-13 from the 3-point range in the second half.

On the flip side, Kansas State (3-2) struggled to find the bottom of the net. The Wildcats shot a season-low 35.1% from the field, when its previous low was 41.5% in their season-opening loss to South Dakota State. In their three previous wins, they shot 49.2% or better.

articles.title: Nicolas Cage on his John Madden misfire: "I'm not Frank Caliendo"
articles.summary: This whole thing is antithetical to my identity.
articles.body:
This whole thing is antithetical to my identity.

That's the one line that resonates most strongly in the new Madden movie. Because it's exactly what John Madden would say if he saw it.

It's bad. It's very bad. Anyone who says it's good has no taste and/or an agenda that involves the strategic application of lips to asses.

The biggest problem is Nicolas Cage as John Madden. Anyone who vividly remembers the unique charisma of John Madden knows instantly that nothing about Cage's portrayal reflects the true nature, spirit, and demeanor of one of the most important and impactful figures in the entire history of the sport of football.

Cage, who seems to realize that his portrayal missed not only the bull's-eye but also the entire wall on which the dart board was mounted, has defended the outcome by peering down his nose at the sports world.

" He was not on my radar ," Cage said of Madden, via Kirsten Chuba of the Hollywood Reporter . "I was growing up watching black-and-white Orson Welles movies and Fellini movies and Bruce Lee. I wasn't interested in team sports whatsoever."

"I'm someone that likes to stay out of his comfort zone and take a risk, I said yes, because that would be a transformation," Cage explained regarding the decision to attempt to play the towering, iconic figure. "It would be something where I might learn a few things, taking on this character who is really nothing like me."

The audience has learned that Cage's interpretation is nothing like Madden.

"That's what acting's about," Cage said. "I'm not an impressionist, I'm not Frank Caliendo. I lean more towards being a surrealist, meaning I like to get a concept of a personality and then dig deep and see what I can locate emotionally with my imagination and my psyche and filter it through the cadence and the appearance, within reason, of John Madden. I'm trying to give you an evocation, more or less, or an interpretation."

The problem was it wasn't even "within reason." It was without reason. And the entire film was beyond unreasonable.

And I like Nicolas Cage. He was brilliant in Moonstruck . He won an Oscar for Leaving Las Vegas . And The Family Man remains a highly underrated holiday film.

Still, to quote another holiday film, "They can't all be winners." Cage's role in Madden as John Madden is not.

I only met John Madden once. I watched him on TV for decades. I've heard plenty of stories about him from people who worked with him at NBC. And I'm confident that he would be livid about this film.

"That's not me," he'd say. "Not even close."

Or, perhaps, "This whole thing is antithetical to my identity."

articles.title: Saturday Predictions: Florida
articles.summary: What says our writing staff?
articles.body:
Vanderbilt can still, technically, get bowl eligible but needs wins in its two remaining games to get there. There were signs of life against Alabama last week but an inability to find the end zone meant a 21-6 loss.

Saturday's visit to Florida in theory presents a beatable opponent, but do our writers think it will actually happen? Let's find out!

If I squint, and I mean really squint, I can see our strengths countering their strengths and our weaknesses mitigated by their weaknesses. Might need to squint whilst being blinded by the daylight savings time sun each day on my commute to and from work level squint to do it, but there is a level of squinting that can allow you to see it. It exists, I tell you!

George Costanza spotting dimes without his glasses level squinting.

The Jorts offense is basically a "Give it to Jadan Baugh" or "Where's Baugh? Ah, give it to a different RB" scheme. I don't know if you managed to see any positives in our loss to the Gumps, but we were pretty good at stopping the run, no? And though The Jorts do have one strong WR, their QB… is not so good.

Now read that while really squinting and also on some pretty strong hallucinogens.

The Pick: Fuck it, why not? Vanderbilt 17, Florida 13. (Now watch it be like 70-0 Jorts, as Baugh goes all Deuce McCallister on our asses and our O-line alternates between penalties and matador cape swinging on every damned play all game.)

The SEC Upset Pick of the Week: I don't know about you, but I'm tired of all these OK Boomers complaining about flights being down and so will decide to, oh God, prefer the Milkman Cult to shut them up? None of these are good choices. Give me Texas They and Them (+7.5) over Texas's hat, but also remember that I am in last place in the gambling without any money on it contest on this very website.

Losing to Alabama 21-6 is not a terrible result. It was extremely frustrating watching the offense fall flat on their face over and over, whether by poor execution, dumb penalties, or strange playcalls. On a day where Alabama was held to less than 100 yards from their first 5 offensive possessions and had 0 points, the offense let the defense down. It has been a weird world watching Vanderbilt fans understandably turn against Offensive Coordinator Tim Beck, who many of us thought was an elite OC after his first two seasons on West End with Diego Pavia. His inability to find a way to get the most out of a good RB group and an extremely talented young QB is concerning. They also appeared to have coached any and all risk taking out of Jared Curtis.

Florida is also struggling on offense. They have scored 17, 19, 27, 8, 7, and 21 points in their 6 games since the start of October. Their last game of September was the 52-28 beatdown of Ole Miss. Meanwhile, Vanderbilt's defense has looked much improved since the bye week.

In what will likely be a painfully low-scoring game, I am going to be hopeful. The offense is going to find just enough, whether it is a handful of grinding drives into FG range or a couple explosive plays. The defense stands tall in the Swamp.

The SEC Upset Pick of the Week: LSU is going to lose again. The Lane Train is going to be completely off the rails and in a flaming heap beside the tracks. Why are they favorites on the road?

If we can score a touchdown, I think we have a shot. If we can't, then yeah it'll be Gators by a tooth. Someone ina mailbag asked if we should have taken a bunch of slightly better players or 1 Jared Curtis, and (while I don't think that was an option we actually had) I'm starting to feel like a bunch of slightly better players would do us more good than this Curtis guy, who I'm predicting throws a pick or fumbles or can't ever seem to find an open guy this weekend.

The SEC Upset Pick of the Week: Apparently Missourah ( spits ) is favored over Big Ugly Blue School? Seems a little strange, but maybe I'm out of the know. I'm still taking Krogertucky.

If it's not obvious yet, I have completely moved on to basketball season. As such, I will be watching, but primarily watching, like, the Division III football playoffs. Vanderbilt will keep things close-ish, probably settle for a few Brock Taylor field goals when drives are left unfinished, and we will be as disappointed as we are annually with Thanksgiving turkey when we could have picked another protein.

The SEC Upset Pick of the Week: You know how much I hate THEM (+1.5) being my upset pick? Yeah, but I also hate Lane Kiffin almost as much.

articles.title: Mizzou cruises to fourth straight win, beats Le Moyne
articles.summary: The Tigers’ homestand continued with another comfortable buy game victory
articles.body:
A corgi named Maggie draped herself in glory during halftime Friday night at Mizzou Arena.

The dog bested several of her fluffy corgi contestants in a race that went hilariously awry.

Each corgi was meant to dash from one baseline to the other in a display of canine athleticism. Instead, most of them never reached the near free throw line, spreading out in every direction except the one intended for them until Maggie finally put an end to the chaos by crossing the finish line.

It was an amusing and heartwarming event that underlined why dogs are known as 'man's best friend.'

It was also arguably the most entertaining moment in a night that also featured another comfortable non-conference victory for Missouri as the Tigers won a contest of their own against Le Moyne, 91-64.

The Dolphins raised some eyebrows early, taking a one-point lead into the first media timeout thanks to a pair of triples.

MU responded with a 7-0 surge over the span of roughly a minute-and-a-half coming out of the break to take control and never looked back.

That run was the first of five long scoring streaks that helped the Tigers establish and then expand their advantage. The longest of those runs happened when Mizzou put 12 unanswered points on the scoreboard to hold a 49-21 lead heading into halftime.

MU made full use of its sizable height and athleticism advantage, physically overpowering Le Moyne. Mizzou finished the night with a 34-22 advantage in points in the paint and won the rebounding battle handily.

The Tigers also utilized their length to apply pressure defensively and pushed the ball in transition, forcing 16 Dolphins turnovers and collecting 26 points off those giveaways.

Le Moyne largely kept pace during the second half, but MU reached its expected margin with a 27-point win.

Jason Crowe Jr. and Bryson Tiller tied for Mizzou's team lead with 18 points apiece. Tiller had an especially impressive performance, going 7-of-13 from the field while scoring at all three levels.

Toni Bryant, Kennard Davis Jr. and Jamier Jones joined their teammates in double figures. Davis also reached a major milestone in the final minute of action, scoring his 1,000th career point on a free throw and finishing with 13 points on the night.

MU's homestand continues Tuesday, when the Tigers host Evansville. That matchup tips off at 8 p.m. and will stream on SEC Network+.

articles.title: Giants bring back reliever Camilo Doval, let infielder Christian Koss go
articles.summary: Among a flurry of minor moves on Friday, the San Francisco Giants re-signed former closer Camilo Doval and designated infielder Christian Koss for assignment...
articles.body:
The San Francisco Giants brought back an old friend and parted ways with one on Friday. They also tendered contracts to their three other arbitration eligible players with a contract agreement to be determined.

Reliever Camilo Doval and the Giants agreed to a one-year contract to avoid arbitration worth $6.3 million, a source confirmed to the Chronicle.

Doval had been traded to the New York Yankees at the 2025 trade deadline. The Yankees then traded him to the Pittsburgh Pirates, who designated him for assignment in September. The pitching-starved Giants claimed Doval off waivers , and he'll stay with the team that signed him as a teenage international free agent.

Infielder Christian Koss was designated for assignment Tuesday to make room on the 40-man roster for their Rule 5 protections.

Koss grew up a Giants fan in Southern California and was a feel-good story in 2025 when he earned an Opening Day roster spot as a non-roster invitee out of spring training. He's a strong defensive infielder who can move all over the diamond and is quick on the bases, but his role off the bench didn't stick. He appeared in 70 games this season, batting .217.

Those protections were left-handed pitcher Henry Lalane and right-handed pitchers Marty Gair and Josh Bostick. Wick was non-tendered and became a free agent. The Giants acquired Lalane and Gair at last year's trade deadline, Lalane from the Yankees for outfielder Heliot Ramos and Gair as part of the Luis Arraez trade with the Philadelphia Phillies .

The Giants could use Doval's stuff - his high-velocity, nasty-moving pitches that he struggled to command toward at his low points - in what they hope to be a revamped bullpen. Doval will return to the roster with his friend Randy Rodriguez, who was also tendered a contract in his first year of arbitration eligibility, to boost the back end of the bullpen.

Though both have closed for the Giants, neither is expected to be the 2027 Giants closer when the season begins (whenever that may be, CBA depending). Rodriguez was closing in late 2025 when his elbow started barking and he was forced to undergo Tommy John surgery. He will ease his way back into high-leverage spots in his first action post-surgery.

President of baseball operations Buster Posey said the team is on the hunt for a closer and more arms to bolster a disappointing pitching staff.

The Giants also tendered a contract to Casey Schmitt , who is generating interest on the trade market . Schmitt is estimated to earn $2.5 million, according to the yearly MLB Trade Rumor projection.

Left-handed reliever Sam Hentges was also tendered a contract, projected to earn $2 million. Rodriguez is estimated to earn $800,000. Outfielder Victor Bericoto and pitcher Rowan Wick were also non-tendered, though Bericoto is expected to sign a minor league contract with the Giants to return.

Wick had an odd stint with the Giants. He signed in February while still on the mend from Tommy John surgery he underwent during his time with the Yokohama DeNA BayStars the year prior.

Wick never pitched for the Giants: his club option was declined in November, he was designated for assignment on Tuesday and ultimately non-tendered, making him a free agent.

articles.title: Carmelo Anthony takes down Ravens’ Marlon Humphrey on IG after ‘criminals’ comment
articles.summary: Carmelo Anthony delivered a pointed message to Marlon Humphrey after the Baltimore Ravens cornerback sparked backlash with controversial remarks about his ho...
articles.body:
Carmelo Anthony delivered a pointed message to Marlon Humphrey after the Baltimore Ravens cornerback sparked backlash with controversial remarks about his hometown. This turned an already turbulent week for the franchise into a bigger off-field distraction . Humphrey was deactivated for Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Carolina Panthers by head coach Jesse Minter. That's after Humphrey joked on 'The Marlon Humphrey Show' that Baltimore was "best at making criminals."

The veteran later apologized. However, Anthony, a West Baltimore native and NBA legend, made it clear that the damage extended beyond a simple locker-room explanation. In a six-slide Instagram statement , Anthony reflected on growing up on Myrtle Avenue, losing friends to street violence, and witnessing people he cared about struggle against systemic barriers. While acknowledging Humphrey's apology, Anthony pushed back against the idea that expressing regret was enough to repair the relationship with the city.

"Marlon, I see the apology. I'll take it, man to man. But Baltimore has been apologized to its whole life. Apologies don't build anything. Presence does… You don't get to rep Baltimore on Sundays and talk about it like an outsider on Wednesday," Anthony wrote.

He also highlighted Baltimore's accomplishments. Anthony pointed to its teachers, coaches, returning citizens, Olympians, Hall of Famers, and boxing champion Gervonta "Tank" Davis as examples of what the city truly represents. Anthony closed by urging Humphrey to accept Mayor Brandon Scott's invitation to meet with formerly incarcerated community mentors. He even offered to join him in person so they could speak directly to Baltimore's youth. The controversy arrives during a difficult Ravens campaign, with Baltimore falling to 4-6 amid a five-game losing streak, injuries, and Lamar Jackson's absence.

articles.title: ‘Probably Be the Next QB of the Colts’ — Former NFL Scout Names NFC Franchise’s Backup As Indianapolis’ Daniel Jones Replacement in 2027
articles.summary: Thursday night turned out to be Daniel Jones’ last game with the Indianapolis Colts, and it was one to forget. He completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards wit...
articles.body:
Thursday night turned out to be Daniel Jones' last game with the Indianapolis Colts, and it was one to forget. He completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards with an interception and no touchdowns in a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans. The loss dropped Indianapolis to 3-8 and left its playoff chances all but gone.

On Friday, head coach Shane Steichen announced that the Colts are waiving Jones and giving the job to Anthony Richardson Sr. The move comes 11 starts into the two-year, $88 million contract Jones signed in the offseason.

Former NFL scout John Middlekauff already has a landing spot in mind for the 29-year-old QB: backing up in San Francisco after Mac Jones leaves.

John Middlekauff Sees Daniel Jones as a Long-Term Backup

Speaking on "3 & Out With John Middlekauff," the former scout started with a quick prediction: "[Daniel] will play somewhere next week, would be my guess."

His longer view runs through San Francisco's quarterback room.

"It hit me last night: I bet he's the 49ers' backup when Mac Jones leaves. He'll [Mac Jones] probably be the next QB of the Colts for like $7 million, and he'll [Daniel Jones] be the 49ers' backup for like $2 million, which is probably his future," Middlekauff said .

Middlekauff's prediction depends on Mac Jones leaving first. The No. 15 overall pick in the 2021 draft is on San Francisco's active roster and could become a free agent in the 2027 offseason unless the team signs him to a new deal.

The former scout then pointed to two quarterbacks who followed a similar path.

"Matt Schaub did this, Joe Flacco did this, and those guys were way better players in their prime. But my guess is he'll be a backup for a long time."

Both Schaub and Flacco went from longtime starters to backups. Schaub took over for an injured Flacco as the Baltimore Ravens' starter during the 2015 season.

Daniel has bounced back from a midseason exit before. The New York Giants drafted him sixth overall out of Duke in 2019, benched him, and granted his request for a release in November 2024. He joined the Minnesota Vikings and finished that season there.

Indianapolis gave him a one-year, $14 million contract for 2025, and he took the starting job from Richardson. The Colts were 8-4 when a torn Achilles ended his season.

Shane Steichen Explains Decision To Move On From Jones

This season, Daniel started all 11 games and completed 205 of 351 passes (58.4%) for 1,974 yards with seven touchdowns and 13 interceptions. He was sacked 27 times.

Through Week 11, his 65.4 passer rating ranks 31st among 31 qualified quarterbacks. He also ranks No. 34 with a PFN QB Impact Score of 62.1.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Steichen spoke warmly on Friday about the quarterback he was letting go. "I can't say enough good things about Daniel, just the ultimate competitor, ultimate teammate," the head coach said.

The release is the latest shake-up in a season in which Indianapolis traded Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs before the Nov. 10 deadline.

"I think there's a lot of factors that played into it. Obviously, the quarterback takes a lot of the blame. That's the business that we're in. But things just didn't work out," Steichen said . "And like I said, I got so much respect for him and everything that he meant to this organization and the way he worked."

Richardson, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 draft, went 0 for 2 in relief Thursday and has not started since Week 16 of the 2024 season. He has completed 50.6% of his passes over 19 career games.

"I talked to Anthony today. I told him, obviously, he'll be the starter versus the Giants," Steichen said.

Behind Richardson, the Colts' only other active quarterback is second-year pro Riley Leonard. "There's, obviously, a world in which Riley could play as well, so we'll evaluate that each and every week throughout the season," the coach said.

For now, the Colts are going with Richardson, who starts Nov. 29 against the Giants.

articles.title: What we learned from UConn women’s basketball bounce-back win over Seton Hall
articles.summary: UConn women’s basketball gets a much-needed win over Seton Hall in the Huskies' Big East opener. Here are the biggest takeaways.
articles.body:
HARTFORD — How did UConn respond to one of the worst losses in recent memory?

How about opening conference play with a 40-point victory .

Following a disappointing 18-point loss to Louisville the previous Sunday, the Huskies demolished visiting Seton Hall 83-43 in their Big East opener at PeoplesBank Arena in Hartford on Friday, Nov. 20.

Jovana Popovic led the way with 20 points, 5 rebounds and 3 assists. Blanca Quiñonez added 18 points off the bench, and Sarah Strong chipped in 13 points.

Here are the biggest takeaways from Friday's win:

Check out our UConn women's basketball vs Seton Hall photo gallery

Blanca Quiñonez back on track for UConn women's basketball

It's been an up-and-down start to the season for the sophomore star.

After posting 21 points against Iowa three games ago, the Ecuadorian forward score just two points over the next two games.

Quiñonez shook off her cold stretch in the first quarter of Friday's game. She scored 11 of her 18 points through the first 10 minutes on 5-of-6 shooting.

Quiñonez ended the game hitting two of her three 3-point attempts and registered a plus-minus rating of +25.

She was a threat on the defensive end as she recorded three blocks and three steals.

The reigning national player of the year didn't need to score 30 points to win this game, but she did a little bit of everything to keep her team engaged against a lesser opponent.

Strong shot just 5-of-16 from the field but had seven rebounds, dished out 5 assists, recorded 4 steals and blocked 2 shots.

She was everywhere on defense, directing traffic while helping on the weakside to hold Seton Hall to 42 points in the paint.

While it was Seton Hall, there was no doubt UConn had one of its most complete defensive performances of the season.

The Huskies held Seton Hall to just 27.6% shooting from the field and 28% from the 3-point line. UConn forced 25 turnovers that led to 25 points.

Leading scorer Savannah Catalon had 14 points, but no other Seton Hall player had more than eight.

Guard Kayleigh Heckel was a last-minute scratch after playing 13 minutes against Louisville.

In her place, UConn coach Geno Auriemma used guards Morgan Cheli and Kelis Fisher in her place.

Cheli played 13 minutes, but was mostly a non-factor having missed her only shot attempt. Fisher got some run in the second half and scored 11 points but also had three turnovers.

articles.body:
RICHMOND, Ky. (AP) — Sam Donald had 24 points in Bellarmine's 79-76 win against Eastern Kentucky on Friday.

Donald added eight rebounds and three steals for the Knights (2-5). Tyler Doyle scored 16 points while going 6 of 11 and 3 of 4 from the free-throw line. Kenyon Goodin shot 2 for 8 (1 for 5 from 3-point range) and 8 of 10 from the free-throw line to finish with 13 points.

Drae Vasser led the way for the Colonels (4-2) with 22 points and two steals. His 35-foot, 3-point heave at the buzzer was the game's final points.

Damone King added 16 points, five assists and two steals for Eastern Kentucky. Shadrak Lasu finished with 10 points and six rebounds.

articles.title: Michigan State hockey embarrassed by Michigan on Friday night
articles.summary: It was an embarrassing night for Michigan State in Ann Arbor, falling to Michigan, 5-1.
articles.body:
It was an embarrassing night for Michigan State hockey on Friday afternoon, after going down to Ann Arbor and getting dominated by the Wolverines, 5-1.

From the opening drop of the puck, Michigan State was lethargic on the ice, unable to match the energy and the play of Michigan. While the games shot total were a tied 38-38 overall, the play felt slanted towards the Michigan State end of the ice.

The lone goal for the Spartans came by way of Cullen Potter, and was assisted by Tommy Bleyl and Jack Hextall.

In the third period, a fight broke out between the Spartans and Wolverines, with both teams having players leave their benches to join in the melee. The result of this scuffle will almost certainly end in suspensions for both teams, and will be something to monitor ahead of tomorrow's series finale.

The Spartans and Wolverines will head to East Lansing for a battle in game two at 6 p.m. inside of Munn Ice Arena.

articles.title: Wilkinson hits 8 3-pointers and helps No. 20 Arkansas beat Mississippi Valley State 92-48
articles.summary: (AP) — Jeremiah Wilkinson scored 28 points and Billy Richmond III added 18 as No. 20 Arkansas defeated Mississippi Valley State 92-48 on Friday night.
articles.body:
FAYETTEVILLE, Ark. (AP) — Jeremiah Wilkinson scored 28 points and Billy Richmond III added 18 as No. 20 Arkansas defeated Mississippi Valley State 92-48 on Friday night.

Wilkinson shot 8 of 16 from 3-point range, tying for seventh place in school history for 3-pointers made. He made four of the five baskets in the second half as Arkansas (4-2) stretched its lead from 16 points to 25 in the first four minutes.

Richmond's 18 points came on 7-for-9 shooting. He added three steals.

The Razorbacks went on a 19-3 run midway through the first half to open a 20-point lead with 7:41 left. The Delta Devils went scoreless from 10:26 to 4:17, missing eight straight field goals and committing three turnovers as Arkansas seized control.

The Razorbacks shot 17 for 32 and carried a 43-25 lead into the break. Seven of Arkansas' 17 field goals were 3-pointers and eight were dunks. The Razorbacks finished with 13 dunks and 15 3s among their 35 field goals.

Razorbacks freshman guard Jordan Smith Jr., a five-star recruit, did not play because of wrist inflammation. Fellow freshman Davion Thompson, who classified up a year to play in college this season, played in place of Smith and became the youngest player in Arkansas history to start a The 17-year-old finished with 13 points and 11 assists.

Caleb Cameron led Mississippi Valley State (0-5) with 16 points.

Mississippi Valley State: At New Mexico on Wednesday.

Arkansas: Faces Michigan State in Detroit on Thursday.

articles.title: Analyst reveals Duke Blue Devils’ most pressing current concern
articles.summary: Jon Scheyer and the Duke Blue Devils are going through a shaky start five games into the 2026-27 season. This resulted in one basketball analyst providing in...
articles.body:
Jon Scheyer and the Duke Blue Devils are going through a shaky start five games into the 2026-27 season. This resulted in one basketball analyst providing insight into what has held back Duke early into the year.

Scheyer has been the Blue Devils' head coach since 2022, going through his fifth season at the helm. He stands out as one of the best coaches in the nation, having led them to the Final Four in 2025.

However, Duke has an intriguing test on its hands. Even though they have talents at the guard spot with Cayden Boozer and Caleb Foster, they are dealing with depth issues as it puts them to the test throughout non-conference action. Even college basketball analyst Chris Walker pointed this out to be a big concern about the team's ceiling with the point guard position being a weakness.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"If you're Duke right now, you're worried about the point guard position, right? [Cayden] Boozer, [Caleb] Foster…in college basketball, you got to have a big-time guard, and that's the one thing I think they're struggling. They're a little bit deficient. I'm sure Scheyer will get it going, though," Walker said.

Duke has historically shined as one of the top teams in the nation. However, if the guard play continues to be inconsistent, it would their doom their chances of having a case as possible national championship contenders this season.

Duke has a 3-2 record five games into the season. They started the campaign dominantly with blowouts against Army and Coastal Carolina. However, they took a step back by losing 79-73 to the Michigan State Spartans. They rebounded with a 90-47 rout over SIUE, but they regressed with a 99-78 blowout loss to the Illinois Fighting Illini.

The Blue Devils will look to bounce back in their next matchup, being at home. They host the Washington State Cougars as tip-off commences on Nov. 21 at 11 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Hawks notch road win at Xavier, 83-65
articles.summary: Isaia Howard had a career high 24 points with Trevin Jirak adding 21 in a big road victory for the Hawks at Xavier
articles.body:
After a week where Iowa lost two in a row and saw the football team get jumped in the CFP standings, it felt like a bit of a nadir in the sports landscape. That changed tonight as the Hawkeyes (3-2) were boosted past Xavier (5-1) in a dominant road victory, 83-65.

It started off shaky enough, with Mike Nwoko making three straight 3s for the Musketeers and an and-1 layup for their first 11 points of the game. After Ben McCollum cycled centers – first Andrew McKeever and then Cam Manyawu – the offense was put on jet fuel behind Trevin Jirak who had 14 first half points on 5/5 shooting (including 4 threes). Jirak's 3rd three inside of 90 seconds gave the Hawks a lead they would never relinquish. He finished with 21 on 8/10 shooting

The man of the second half was Isaia Howard, who used a desperation three at the end of the first half to set his night on fire (5 of 6 from deep). He finished with an insane stat line of 24 points (a career high), 8 boards, 5 assists, and 3 steals. Oh yeah, and no turnovers (Iowa had just 4 on the game). Jirak's extended minutes provided a lot of spacing for the Hawks and Howard was able to take advantage with 3 of 4 shooting inside throughout the second half.

Both teams were on fire from three throughout the first half with Iowa going 9/13 while the Musketeers started 7/10. While Xavier was starting hot, Iowa did well to make sure that contested threes were the best shots they could get as the Hawks continually defended the rim in excellent fashion. They had 3 blocks and allowed 5/9 on layups/dunks in the first half. Perhaps even more impressive is how they forced Xavier into a ton of jumpers the rest of the way, with only 1 layup attempt in the second half…which came with less than 2 minutes remaining.

A huge reason for that is Iowa's backend communication. Cooper Koch has picked up where he left off as a defender and is regularly in the paint, making opponents question whether it's worth taking it to the rim. When they do, his verticality has been superb. Throughout the game Iowa was able to make that area of the game tough, and when the three stopped falling for them, it really shut Xavier's water off.

On the flip side, Iowa did not settle for 3s after starting the game incredibly hot. In fact, they used that spacing to drive and kick and drive some more. After going 6/15 from 2 in the first half, they made 13/18 in the second half. Just beautiful basketball.

Kael Combs led the way in the category with 7 assists in a mostly ho-hum game for him. Ty'reek Coleman joined Howard with 5, despite playing just 13 minutes in the game. In fact, every guy who saw the floor, except for Jaidyn Coon & Peyton McCollum, had an assist.

It's going to be really interesting to see if this can continue against like competition. If it can, it will be okay if Iowa never has a constant leading scorer given Howard was the 6th guy in 6 games to lead Iowa in scoring.

articles.title: No. 12 Kentucky WBB cracks Marshall’s zone behind Me’Arah O’Neal and Ajsa Sivka
articles.summary: No. 12 Kentucky shook off early turnovers and a cold start from deep to beat Marshall 85-49.
articles.body:
For the first five minutes or so on Friday night, Marshall looked like it might have found a blueprint to frustrate No. 12 Kentucky.

The Thundering Herd sat back in a zone and watched Kentucky cough up a few too many careless passes. But as expected, Kentucky figured it out, and the game was over almost immediately.

Once the Wildcats stopped rushing passes and started slicing through the gaps in Marshall's zone, the margin ballooned in a hurry.

The Cats walked into the locker room up 44-20, and it only got better from there.

What separated Friday night from a sloppy trap game was how quickly Kentucky adjusted when the perimeter shooting went cold. The Wildcats came in riding a streak of three straight games with at least 10 made threes, and though they finished one shy of a fourth at 9-of-29 (31%), they didn't let a cool night from deep stall the offense.

The Wildcats shot 22-of-37 (59.5%) on two-point attempts and piled up 36 points in the paint. Just as important, the early ball-handling hiccups vanished as the game settled in. Kentucky finished with only nine turnovers against 17 assists while forcing 16 Marshall giveaways, which led to 22 points on turnovers.

A big part of that was Asja Sivka and Me'Arah O'Neal.

In the first half, it was Asja Sivka who broke Marshall's zone apart. She poured in 15 of her 17 points before halftime. Sivka finished 6-of-8 from the floor and 3-of-4 from deep, giving Kentucky the exact spacing it needed to pull Marshall's defenders out of the paint.

Once the floor opened up, Me'Arah O'Neal went to work.

She scored a game-high 21 points, going 8-of-12 from the field (8-of-10 inside the arc) and 7-of-9 at the stripe while adding nine rebounds and four blocks.

With those two carrying the heavy load, the rest of the roster simply filled the gaps.

Strack managed 10 points and nine rebounds, and Emily McDonald gave the bench a jolt, drilling 4-of-6 from three-point range for 12 points with zero turnovers.

As sharp as Kentucky's offense looked after the first quarter, the defense was just as decisive.

Marshall's leading scorer, Olivia Olson, never got comfortable. The Cats had her in foul trouble and she ended up finishing with just seven points on 3-of-11 shooting and zero assists.

Without Olson orchestrating the attack, the Thundering Herd (5-2) managed only six assists all night and shot 31% from the field (18-of-58) and 25% from three (5-of-20).

Cassie Gallagher was the lone bright spot for Marshall, putting up 15 points on 6-of-16 shooting (3-of-7 from deep).

With the homestand wrapped up, Kentucky gets a full week off to rest and enjoy some time with family before heading south.

The Wildcats will be back on the floor on Black Friday, Nov. 27, taking on Maine in the Daytona Beach Classic at 4:45 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Tennessee soccer defeats Liberty in NCAA Tournament behind Ines Derrien's two goals
articles.summary: Tennessee soccer took advantage of its hosting bid in the NCAA Tournament, and defeated Liberty 3-2 at Regal Stadium.
articles.body:
Tennessee soccer hasn't touched the field in 19 days, but all rust was quickly knocked off with a goal 35 seconds into the match Nov. 20 at Regal Stadium.

Though Liberty answered quickly, two goals from Ines Derrien, and a goal from freshman Olivia Feagin vaulted the Lady Vols to a 3-2 win over Liberty in the first round of the NCAA Tournament. Tennessee advances to the Round of 32 to face No. 1 Ohio State on Nov. 27.

"Our team has had some adversity as of late," Tennessee interim coach Jonathan Morgan said. "It's been a challenge for us. However, super proud of our kids, super proud of their resiliency and just their commitment for the last 19 days since we had some changes here."

The Lady Vols haven't played since Nov. 1 when they beat Oklahoma, but missed the SEC Tournament. That prompted a change in leadership when then-coach Joe Kirt was fired the next day. Morgan earned the interim tag, and helped rally the Lady Vols through the emotional turmoil.

"We lost our leader," Morgan said. "We lost a friend, (we lost a) mentor... I think the first couple of days after the announcement, I think all of us kept waking up just like, 'Was that real? Or was that a dream?' Just didn't feel right."

The emotions didn't carry into match play.

Just 35 seconds into the match, Derrien earned a penalty kick and cashed in for an early lead. Liberty answered at the 5:01 mark with a score off the corner kick for the equalizer by Sallie Garner.

Derrien had a snuck her second goal of the match beneath the crossbar to put Tennessee ahead 2-1 in the 26th minute. The goal was her fifth of the season, marking the first multi-goal performance for Derrien since Aug. 17, 2025, while at USC.

"I think the entire team stepped up when it mattered," Derrien said. "This is kind of like our season. The whole past season, we kind of just not think about right now. We're thinking about the postseason. It's like a fresh start for us."

Feagin put in Tennessee's third goal of the first half with a soft touch off a teardrop pass from Shae O'Rourke in front of the net. The Lady Vols led 3-1 in the 42nd minute, scoring three times on four shots on goal.

The Lady Flames entered the match conceding just 0.62 goals per match with 12 shutouts. Liberty had allowed three goals or more one time this season — a 4-3 win over George Mason on Sept. 6. Tennessee, which averages only 1.62 goals per match, scored three goals in the first 45 minutes of soccer Friday.

Liberty didn't go down without a late surge, though. Halle Engle snuck a ball past Cayden Norris to bring the Lady Flames within a goal with 20 minutes remaining in the match. That was the last goal Norris conceded before the final horn sounded, pushing the Lady Vols to the second round.

"We expected to have a chance to play in the postseason," Norris said. "We put the work in these past 19 days and we set ourselves up enough to get a bid. So I think, considering the work we put in, I expected to be here."

The program's new coach, Richard Moodie , coached Purdue to a 4-0 win over Southern Illinois on Friday. If both the Lady Vols and Boilermakers advance to the Sweet 16, Tennessee would be facing its future coach.
